newsitem.title: USA: Boston Chicken to cut jobs, take Q2 charge.
newsitem.headline: Boston Chicken to cut jobs, take Q2 charge.

text.p: Boston Chicken Inc will cut 115 positions, or 23 percent of the workforce at its Golden, Colorado, headquarters, and take a pretax, severance-related charge of about $4 million, or $0.04 a share, in the second quarter, a spokeswoman said Monday.
The spokeswoman also told Reuters the restaurant chain was comfortable with analysts' second-quarter earnings estimate of $0.33 a share, excluding the $0.04 per share charge.
But the company is not comfortable with the consensus forecast of $1.37 a share for the full year, she said. Boston Chicken did not provide further guidance on the 1997 estimates.

The job cuts will result in cost savings of $5 million to $6 million for the rest of this year, or $0.05 to $0.06 a share. On an annualized basis, the savings will amount to about $7 million to $10 million, spokeswoman Karen Rugen said.
Boston Chicken said the staff cuts would not affect employees at Einstein/Noah Bagel Corp, in which it holds a majority interest. The cuts also will not affect employees in its retail stores.
Boston Chicken, which operates 1,159 Boston Market retail food stores, will also restructure the administrative and support functions of its 15 "area developers," or franchisees.
The four highest-performing area developers now will provide administrative and support services to the other franchisees, Boston Chicken said.

The area developers, which operate as separate, private companies, will save up to $30 million a year by cutting duplicated services. The area developers, not Boston Chicken, will see the savings, Rugen said.
Staff reductions in the field will take another 60 to 90 days to evaluate. The area developers will determine any staff cuts once their reorganization is completed, Rugen said.

Boston Market said it was examining "ready-to-heat" meals, or fresh food that consumers can take home and heat at their leisure. The company will test-market "ready-to-heat" meals in Atlanta and one market in the Midwest shortly.

Demand for ready-to-heat meals appears to be strong outside the United States, Rugen said. Boston Chicken said it would delay its international expansion until it finalizes it plan for the ready-to-heat product line.
The international expansion, set to begin first in Taiwan, is now slated to begin in late 1998, instead of early next year, Rugen said.
Boston Chicken had expected licensing fees and other revenue from the international expansion to boost 1997 earnings per share by about four to five percent.
In view of the delay, the company will not realize any benefit from the expansion until late 1998, Rugen said.
Boston Chicken will also review its 1997 development plan. That may result in a slowdown of store expansion for 1997, but no decision has been made yet.
The company had expected to add 300 stores in 1997. Rugen said 72 stores had already been opened in the first quarter and 60 stores were to be added in the second.
